<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, the most direct evidence is the presence of carbonyl carbon signals in the 13C NMR spectrum, which appear in the characteristic downfield region (~190–220 ppm). By obtaining the 13C NMR spectrum and counting how many distinct signals fall within this range, we can accurately report the number of C=O groups without needing multiple experiments.</thought>
